title: To Pimp a Butterfly
description: Jazz, funk and spoken word fold into a sprawling, furious meditation on fame and Black America.

title: Rumours
description: Breakups, harmonies and flawless soft-rock songwriting from a band falling apart in real time.

title: SOS
description: Twenty-three tracks of heartbreak and bravado, moving from slow-burn R&B to pop-punk.

title: Unknown Pleasures
description: Cold, cavernous post-punk produced by Martin Hannett. The sleeve is a pulsar; the sound is Manchester at night.

title: Abbey Road
description: The last album the Beatles recorded together, closing on a side-two medley that still feels like a farewell.

title: Illmatic
description: Ten tracks, no filler: Queensbridge rendered in dense, cinematic rhymes over Premier and Pete Rock beats.

title: folklore
description: A hushed, woodsy left turn written in lockdown with Aaron Dessner and Jack Antonoff.

title: London Calling
description: Punk breaks out of its own rules: reggae, rockabilly, ska and soul across four restless sides.

title: Calle 13
description: The Puerto Rican duo's debut: playful, filthy, politically sharp reggaeton that refused to sit still.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
description: Time, money, madness and a heartbeat. One of the best-selling and best-sounding records ever pressed.

title: Lemonade
description: Betrayal, rage and reconciliation, told through blues, country, rock and gospel.

title: Ramones
description: Fourteen songs in under half an hour. Three chords, leather jackets, and the blueprint for punk.

title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
description: Anniversary box with the new stereo mix, session outtakes and a hardback book.

title: Lil Boat
description: Bubblegum melodies and sing-song flows from the mixtape that made Yachty a household name.

title: Horses
description: Poetry over garage rock, produced by John Cale. Its first line is still one of the great openings in rock.

title: Nevermind
description: The record that dragged grunge into the mainstream, with Butch Vig's huge, polished guitars.

title: Actually
description: Arch, melancholy synth-pop about money and Thatcher's Britain, featuring Dusty Springfield.

title: Who's Next
description: Synth loops meet power chords. Salvaged from the abandoned Lifehouse project and better for it.

title: Ready to Die
description: Biggie's debut, a cradle-to-grave story told with effortless flow and gallows humour.

title: She's So Unusual
description: Seven-inch reissue of the hits from the debut that gave the world 'Girls Just Want to Have Fun'.

title: On the Beach
description: Ragged, bleak and beautiful. The middle of Young's 'ditch trilogy', long unavailable on vinyl.

title: Some Girls
description: The Stones answer punk and disco at once, with 'Miss You' and 'Beast of Burden'.

title: There's a Riot Goin' On
description: Murky, drum-machine funk that turned the optimism of the sixties inside out.

title: Live Through This
description: Courtney Love's scorched, melodic howl. Sweet hooks with broken glass in them.

title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
description: Drone, noise and tenderness under Warhol's banana. Few bought it; everyone who did started a band.
